# Warm Homes and Energy Conservation Act 2000

The Warm Homes and Energy Conservation Act 2000 is an act of the Parliament of the United Kingdom relating to the reduction of fuel poverty.
Background
David Amess proposed the legislation after one of his constituents died due to hypothermia.
Legislative passage
The legislation was not amended in the House of Lords.
The legislation was supported by the First Blair ministry.
Provisions
The legislation requires that the government do everything "reasonably practicable" to end fuel poverty in England and Wales by 2010 among vulnerable households and by 2016 among all households.
Further developments
The targets set under the legislation were not all met, but it did result in several benefits:
* successful investments in energy efficiency of households
* customer satisfaction
* thermal comfort
* improvements in health
* a "net positive cost curve" which means that it saved more than it cost.
